Profitability and Margin Expansion
The quarterly adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $4.06, up 80% year-over-year, beat the analyst consensus estimate of $3.88. The adjusted EPS rose 18% quarter-over-quarter.
Adjusted gross margin for the quarter expanded 470 basis points Y/Y to 74.5%, supported by favorable product mix and higher revenue.
The quarterly adjusted operating margin increased 880 basis points to 52.3%.
The stock dropped despite the upbeat results, driven by renewed weakness across U.S. equity markets following Monday’s rally courtesy of

children: Analog Devices benefits from Nvidia-driven demand for AI data center and robotics technologies, while Nvidia draws on ADI’s power-management, sensing and connectivity solutions to support its GPU clusters and physical AI systems. Their complementary technologies help improve power efficiency, data processing and real-time sensing across AI infrastructure.
Industrial and AI Data Centers Drive Growth
Industrial revenue, representing 50% of quarterly sales, increased 55% Y/Y, supported by aerospace and defense, automated test equipment (ATE) and electronic test and measurement.
Automotive revenue rose 21%, reflecting demand for connectivity, audio processing and battery management solutions.
Communications revenue surged 81%, with data centers accounting for 83% of the segment and 13% of total sales. Data center revenue more than doubled year over year for the second consecutive quarter.
Consumer revenue increased 7% despite memory-related challenges.
AI, Robotics And Acquisitions Support Growth
CEO and Chair
Vincent Roche
attributed growth to AI infrastructure investment, industrial automation, robotics, defense, health care and automotive technologies.
Roche said the company’s design-in pipeline expanded 40% in fiscal 2026, while more than two-thirds of annual revenue growth came from markets outside AI-centric applications.
The acquisition of
Alif
added AI-focused microcontrollers and fusion processors, while the
Empower
acquisition strengthened Analog Devices’ power-management capabilities for AI infrastructure.
Puccio said the company generated approximately $900 million in revenue synergies from Maxim in fiscal 2026 and expects to exceed $1 billion in fiscal 2027.
Cash Flow and Shareholder Returns
Analog Devices generated $2.34 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, up from $1.70 billion Y/Y.
Free cash flow reached a record $2 billion for the quarter. Capital expenditure for the quarter was $340.23 million.
The company returned $5.4 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases in fiscal 2026.
Cash and short-term investments totaled $5.2 billion at quarter-end.
Fiscal 2027 Outlook and Supply Constraints
Analog Devices forecast first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $4.4 billion, plus or minus $150 million (vs. $4.34 billion
), and adjusted EPS of $3.82, plus or minus 20 cents (versus $3.86 analyst estimate).
Management expects an adjusted operating margin of 50.5%, plus or minus 100 basis points.
The company plans $1.6 billion–$1.9 billion in fiscal 2027 capital expenditures to expand U.S. and European manufacturing capacity.
Puccio identified industry-wide supply constraints across foundries, packaging and assembly, while Roche described packaging as a major bottleneck.
Management expects continued operating leverage and meaningful free-cash-flow growth despite increased investment.
Puccio said demand remains strong, with book-to-bill above one across nearly all end markets and normal order cancellations.
ADI Price Action:
Analog Devices shares were down 16.85% at $314.93 at the time of publication on Tuesday, according to Benzinga Pro data.
